docRequirement: mcp.md:78 — "When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`. The MCP specification uses the name `streamable-http` for this transport, so configurations copied from server documentation work without modification." Every JSON reader of an MCP server entry must treat the `type` value `streamable-http` as exactly equal to `http` (same `url`, `headers`, `oauth`, `timeout`, `alwaysLoad` handling), not as an unknown transport.
current: Four independent readers each hold a closed transport set and none of them knows the alias. (1) The `.mcp.json`/`mcp.json` reader: `packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:118` reads `const type = raw.type;` and `:119` gates on `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse')`; `:144` handles `'ws'`, `:163` handles `undefined|'stdio'`, and `:177` returns `null` for everything else. `parseMcpServersDocument` turns that null into the warning `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<slug>": unsupported MCP server config` (project-config.ts:211) and omits the server from the returned map. Verified by execution, not only by reading: running `parseMcpServersDocument({mcpServers:{alias:{type:'streamable-http',url:'https://mcp.example.com/mcp'},plain:{type:'http',url:'…'}}})` returns `KEYS ["plain"]` and `WARN ["Ignoring .mcp.json server \"alias\": unsupported MCP server config"]` (positive control `plain` survives on the same run). (2) The Claude plugin adapter: `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1030` derives `rawTransport` from `type`/`transport`/shape and `:1040` narrows it to `'stdio'|'http'|'sse'|'ws'`, else `:1043-1045` pushes `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).` and `continue`s. (3) The Codex plugin adapter: `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/codex.ts:905-907` has the same closed set (`stdio|http|sse`). (4) The legacy manifest adapter: `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:1316-1318`, same closed set. Nothing normalizes the alias one layer up: `packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:455-466` JSON.parses the raw file text and hands it straight to `parseMcpServersDocument`, and `loadProjectMcpServers` (project-config.ts:218-236) does the same; `grep -rn -a -i streamable` over non-vendored source finds the token only in docs prose, plan/spec files, and unrelated MCP-SDK class names — there is no alias table anywhere in our own code. One layer down, the pool is fine once the reader is: `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:430` maps `type === 'http'` to the Streamable HTTP client transport, and `SdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:733-735) is a closed `'http' | 'sse'` arm, so the normalized value `'http'` is already the right target. Surfaces affected in this fork: project `<cwd>/.mcp.json` (native-sources.ts:1067), global `<configDir>/mcp.json` (native-sources.ts:906), project `<project>/.nessy-agent/mcp.json` (native-sources.ts:1018) — all three materialize through `parseMcpServersDocument` — plus plugin-bundled `.mcp.json` and inline manifest MCP maps through the adapters.
divergence: One accepted-value delta, not a field-name or semantics delta. The key (`type`), the value semantics (Streamable HTTP), and everything downstream are already correct — only the spelling `streamable-http` is missing from four closed transport sets, so an entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is parsed to `null`/`undefined` and dropped instead of being read as `type: "http"`. No new transport, no new field, no schema change: the alias must collapse to the existing `'http'` value before the transport switch.

change.what: Add the one shared helper the four readers call: `export function normalizeMcpTransportAlias(value: unknown): unknown { return value === 'streamable-http' ? 'http' : value; }` with the `mcp.md:78` sentence quoted above it. This file already exports `mcpToolTimeoutMs`/`expandConfigVariables` and is already imported by project-config.ts:5-9 and format-adapters/claude.ts:110, so no new dependency edge is created. Inlining the ternary at each site is equally acceptable — the helper exists so the four sites cannot drift.

ONE LINE. Replace line 118 `const type = raw.type;` with `const type = normalizeMcpTransportAlias(raw.type);` (add the import to the existing `./server-config-values.ts` import block at :5-9). The existing `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse')` at :119 then narrows the alias to `'http'`, and the returned `{ type, url, headers, oauth, ...timeout, ...pinned }` at :126-133 already carries `'http'`. Do NOT add a fifth arm — an `oauth` object, `timeout` and `alwaysLoad` must all behave exactly as they do for `http`.

ONE LINE. At :1030-1031 wrap the derived value: `const rawTransport = normalizeMcpTransportAlias(stringField(rawServer, 'type') ?? stringField(rawServer, 'transport') ?? (…));` (or apply the ternary to the `type` read alone). The closed-set narrowing at :1040 and the `PluginMcpDescriptor.transport: 'stdio'|'http'|'sse'|'ws'` union (plugins/types.ts:170) stay unchanged. Extend the comment block at :1032-1039, which already cites `mcp.md:322` and `:147`, with `mcp.md:78`.

ONE LINE, consistency only — Codex is not bound by this Claude page, but a Codex plugin bundling a `.mcp.json` hits the same copied-from-server-docs spelling. Apply the same alias to `rawTransport` at :905 before the `stdio|http|sse` narrowing at :906-907. Note in the comment that this is our choice, not a Codex spec requirement (developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins does not mention the alias).
ONE LINE, consistency only. Same alias applied to `rawTransport` at :1316 before the `stdio|http|sse` narrowing at :1317-1318, so a legacy manifest map behaves like the Claude one.

OPTIONAL, and explicitly NOT a security fix — do not file it as one. `:453-456` narrows the declared transport to `stdio|http|sse` and yields `undefined` for the alias, but `transportKind` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-mcp-entries.ts:454-459) falls back to the SHAPE — a server with a `url` is `'remote'` — so the managed allow/deny evaluation (`evaluateManagedMcpServer`, :489-511) already treats a `streamable-http` entry as remote and the `serverUrl` row still binds it. Adding the alias here only makes the cosmetic `mcpTransport` on the panel summary (capabilities/resolver.ts:1650-1655) exact instead of relying on its own `'http'` fallback.

Add the positive path — `parseMcpServersDocument({mcpServers:{docs:{type:'streamable-http',url:'https://mcp.example.com/mcp',headers:{Authorization:'Bearer x'},oauth:{scopes:'read'},timeout:5000,alwaysLoad:true}}})` yields `{type:'http', url, headers, oauth, toolTimeoutMs, alwaysLoad}` with NO warning — and the boundary — an unknown `type` such as `'streamable'` or `'https'` still returns `null` and still warns `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<slug>": unsupported MCP server config`. One table-driven pair is enough; the existing http/sse/ws/stdio cases already cover the rest.
One case asserting a plugin `.mcp.json` entry with `"type": "streamable-http"` imports as a `transport: 'http'` PluginMcpDescriptor with no `plugin.format.*` incomplete diagnostic.

blastRadius: Read-side only, but it crosses two boundaries worth naming. (1) PERSISTENCE — plugin normalization runs at INSTALL time (`PluginInstallService` calls `normalizePluginBundle(staged.rawDirectory, staged.plan.origin, this.adapters, …)`, install-service.ts:196 and :309-314) and the normalized capability set is what gets stored, so already-installed plugins keep their dropped server until they are reinstalled or re-normalized; the fix does not retroactively repair an installed plan. (2) TURN MATERIALIZATION — `parseMcpServersDocument` is called per turn from `materializeSnapshotMcpServers` (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:455-466), so the file-based surfaces heal on the next turn with no migration. Other readers of the same parser: `loadProjectMcpServers` (project-config.ts:218), exercised by packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/base-agent.test.ts:803; and `detectMcpServers` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:109-129), which feeds the pre-trust project-contributions consent list — that list currently omits the alias entry and will start including it, which is the intended change. Downstream of the reader nothing needs touching: `SdkMcpServerConfig` (agent/backend/types.ts:733) is a closed union whose `'http'` arm is the target, `sdkConfigToClientConfig` (mcp-pool.ts:429-435) and `isSdkMcpServerConfig` (mcp-pool.ts:181-184) already accept `'http'`, and `PluginMcpDescriptor.transport` / `PluginConnectorMcpServerDescriptor.transport` (plugins/types.ts:170, :616) already carry `'http'`. No wire/schema/IPC field changes. Existing tests that touch these readers: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/{ws-transport,oauth-config,always-load-config,mcp-server-timeout-config,config-variable-expansion}.test.ts, packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/{claude-mcp-ws,format-adapters}.test.ts. Sibling subsystem deliberately excluded: an MCP *Source*'s own `config.json` spells the key `transport` (packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:151-164 always connects over Streamable HTTP) — it is our format, not a Claude JSON surface, and is out of scope for this page.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. A user pastes the JSON block from an MCP vendor's own quickstart — most publish `"type": "streamable-http"`, which is the MCP spec's name for the transport — into the project `.mcp.json` (or `~/.nessy-agent/mcp.json`, or `<project>/.nessy-agent/mcp.json`). The capability inventory still records the entry (native-sources.ts:493-509 creates one record per declared key regardless of `type`, and resolver.ts:1642-1655 turns that into a catalogue/MCP-panel summary whose transport falls back to `http`), so the server LOOKS configured, but the pool never receives it (runtime-pool-servers.ts:461-466 drops the parsed `undefined`) and none of its tools ever appear. The only diagnosis is the debug-channel line `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` — nothing in the UI says the word `streamable-http`. On top of that, the pre-trust "this project provides N MCP servers" consent list undercounts, because it is built from the same parser (project-contribution-detect.ts:129), so the user approves a project without seeing the server that is being declared. Editing `streamable-http` to `http` by hand fixes it, which is exactly the manual step the doc sentence says should not be needed.
notes: The production delta is two one-line edits (project-config.ts:118, claude.ts:1030); the M rating is for the two optional consistency lines plus the two test cases. Every file cited was read at the lines quoted, and the `.mcp.json` consequence was reproduced by executing the parser under bun (KEYS ["plain"], WARN ["Ignoring .mcp.json server \"alias\": unsupported MCP server config"]) with `plain` as the positive control. The doc sentence was re-fetched with `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md` (1282 lines) and sits verbatim at line 78; the whole line was read — its second sentence reinforces rather than qualifies. Two peripheral points rest on inference, neither load-bearing for the fix: (a) that the Claude Agent SDK's own `.mcp.json` loader honours the alias, which would give the Claude backend only (off by default behind NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE, `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`) a fallback our pool does not have — taken from the doc, not measured against the SDK; (b) that the MCP panel visibly renders a row for the dropped server — inferred from the inventory record (native-sources.ts:493-509) and the resolver summary (resolver.ts:1642-1655), not from a live screenshot; the catalogue-level record itself is verified. Adjacent but separate: the paragraph immediately after line 78 specifies the `url`-without-`type` error message, which is its own finding and is not addressed here.
